summary: 14-day closed-loop AAPS analysis (2026-08-07 to 2026-08-21, BST) on u200 dilute basal profile with FLAT ISF (56 mg/dL/U), 7-segment basal schedule, and UAM-driven micro-bolus meal strategy. Data quality excellent (98.7% CGM coverage). Overall glucose control moderate: 86% time-in-range, but 5.1% time below 70 mg/dL (8 readings < 70, nadir 41) and 8.9% time above 180 mg/dL (12 readings > 250, peak 293). Afternoon hyperglycemia (hour 16 local: 162.8 mg/dL avg, 32.1% above range) is the primary control issue. No carbs logged (0 entries); meal detection relies entirely on UAM. GLP-1 dosed on days 8, 11, 14 (1.25 mg each). Profile changed 2026-08-13 21:23:31; lows immediately followed. Automation is conservative: micro-SMB every 3 min (typical 0.05 U), Dynamic ISF 70% reduces bolus further, Autosens disabled. Declared meal strategy is null. Overall strategy inferred: reactive (no prebolus), 4–20% immediate bolus, 80–96% via progressive micro-SMB over 1–4 hours, no e-carbs. Primary recommendation: enable carb logging immediately, then after 7 days of carb data assess ISF (observed effective ISF 150–180 from therapy windows suggests declared 56 is too low or too high depending on oref1 model clarification; recommend verification via carb-logged bolus response before ISF change). Secondary: review basal segments at 00:00 (0.6 U/h, hour-01 TBR 18.5%) and 16:00 (0.5 U/h drop during peak TAR 32.1%) after carb logging is established. Tertiary: confirm 10h DIA via fasting bolus test, and clarify whether e-carbs will be used for slow-absorbing meals.

Hours 13–17 TAR range 16.6–32.1%, indicating meal inadequately bolused (not basal issue). Evening basal (18:00–23:00): hour-18 elevated (avg 124.2, TAR 11.9%), hour-19 TBR spike (15.3%, avg 105.4; low events post-afternoon high). Hours 20–21 recover (TIR 92.3%, 88.6%). Basal profile structure reasonable; 16:00 drop to 0.5 U/h misaligned with afternoon meal window. Hour-01 TBR and hour-19 TBR spike likely driven by meal dynamics and IOB feedback, not pure basal inadequacy.

analysis_steps.findings: ISF declared as single flat segment: 56 mg/dL/U (00:00 onward). From therapy_response_windows, glucose_change / insulin_units ranges 36–353 mg/dL/U (extreme spread due to meal/IOB confound; median ~150–180). Declared ISF 56 vs. observed 150–180 represents major discrepancy. Interpretation depends on oref1 ISF definition: if higher ISF means more sensitive insulin (1 U lowers glucose more), then observed 150–180 suggests ISF should be 150–180 (not 56). If interpretation is reversed (lower ISF means more sensitive), then 56 is correct and therapy response range is confounded by meal/IOB. Dynamic ISF enabled (70% adjustment) increases effective ISF from 56 to ~80 (formula: 56 × 100/70 ≈ 80). CR declared in 5 segments: 13, 11.1, 13.2, 10.5, 12.6 g/U. CR not used for immediate meal bolus (zero carbs logged, UAM only); real bolus is micro-SMB. DIA declared as 10h (extended, consistent with dilute u200 insulin). Bolus recovery patterns mostly consistent with 10h tail. No evidence contradicts 10h DIA. CR tuning deferred until carbs are logged; ISF verification deferred until carb-logged bolus response clarifies ISF direction.

analysis_steps.findings: Primary issue: No carbs logged (0 entries) for 14 days; UAM is only meal detector, limiting meal bolus sizing, prebolus feasibility, and CR validation. Secondary issue: Afternoon hyperglycemia (hour 16 TAR 32.1%, peak 293 mg/dL) uncontrolled despite automated micro-SMB every 3 minutes; root cause is either (a) meal bolus insufficient due to micro-SMB strategy (80–96% of bolus via 0.05 U per 3-min cycle spread over 1–4 hours), or (b) declared ISF 56 is incorrect (observed effective ISF 150–180 therapy windows suggests ISF model discrepancy requiring clarification). Tertiary issue: Reactive bolus timing (no prebolus observed) leads to overshoot, then aggressive loop correction, then undershoot (hour 19 TBR spike 15.3% post-afternoon high). Quaternary issue: Basal segments 00:00 (0.6 U/h, hour-01 TBR 18.5%) and 16:00 (0.5 U/h drop during peak TAR) show unusual patterns; likely secondary to meal/IOB dynamics rather than basal alone. Conflicting evidence on ISF: observed glucose_change / insulin_units ≈ 150–180 could indicate (H1) declared ISF 56 is too low (insulin too weak), requiring increase, or (H2) therapy responses are confounded by meal IOB overlap and UAM uncertainty, requiring carb logging to clarify. Resolution strategy: (1) Enable carb logging immediately (lowest-risk, highest-information change). (2) After 7 days of carb-logged bolus responses, recalculate implied ISF empirically; use this to inform ISF direction (increase or decrease). (3) After carbs are logged, enable smb_with_cob_enabled=true (allow COB-based SMB), assess prebolus feasibility (meal log time vs. bolus time gap). (4) After ISF and carb-logging stability (1–2 weeks), conduct fasting basal test to isolate basal effects. Order is critical: carb logging first (enables all downstream decisions); ISF change deferred pending carb-logged data.
analysis_steps.evidence: Afternoon TAR 32.1% (hour 16) persists across all 14 days and multiple meal events, pointing to systematic issue (meal bolus strategy or ISF) rather than meal variability. Micro-bolus pattern (0.05 U per 3 min typical) is insufficient to suppress 4-hour meal absorption in real-time (80 cycles × 0.05 U ≈ 4 U total bolus; estimated meal 40–65g carbs suggests 3–5 U needed per CR; marginal). Declared ISF 56 vs. observed 150–180 discrepancy cannot be resolved without carbs (IOB subtraction in algorithm vs. pure ISF effect unknown). Basal-only explanation for hour-16 TAR implausible (basal constant across hours; TAR varies 32.1% hour-16 to 22.6% hour-17, showing meal-driven, not basal-driven). Hour-01 TBR 18.5% and hour-19 TBR spike 15.3% correlate with oscillatory patterns (afternoon high → evening aggressive correction → low), not pure basal inadequacy.

strengths: Excellent data quality and completeness: 98.7% CGM coverage, 5-min cadence, zero invalid/duplicate entries, full profile specification, 24 loop snapshots. No missing telemetry.
Closed-loop system is active and responsive; preventing severe lows. Loop is functional and can be further tuned.
Conservative automation design (micro-SMB every 3 min, 0.05 U per cycle) provides inherent safety margin, prevents large IOB spikes, and detects glucose rises via UAM reliably without carbs.
Time-in-range is 86% (acceptable); good overnight and early-morning control (hours 04–07 TIR 95–98.7%).
Profile fully specified (7 basal, 5 CR, 3 target segments; SMB/UAM/sensitivity all documented). No missing critical settings.
GLP-1 use logged (3 doses visible); provides context for meal absorption variability.
Multiple bolus exceptions visible (2.4 U, 0.65 U); shows system is not mechanically blocked from larger boluses when needed.

issues.title: Afternoon hyperglycemia uncontrolled; hour-16 TAR 32.1%, peak 293 mg/dL; hours 13–17 TAR 16.6–32.1%.
issues.description: Pattern spans all 14 days across multiple meal events (breakfast 08:00–13:00, lunch 13:00–17:00 local). Root causes: (1) Micro-SMB strategy (0.05 U per 3-min cycle, 80 cycles per 4-hour meal ≈ 4 U total, vs. estimated 3–5 U needed for 40–65g carbs) insufficient. (2) ISF declared 56 vs. observed effective 150–180 (therapy_response_windows glucose_change / insulin_units); if 56 is too low, bolus formula undersizes bolus; if 56 is correct and 150–180 is confounded artifact, carb logging will clarify. issues.title: Hypoglycemia clusters after profile change (2026-08-13 17:04–17:14, 2026-08-14 18:04–18:14, lows 41–51 mg/dL) and hour-19 TBR spike 15.3% post-afternoon high.
issues.description: 5.1% TBR (14-day), 8 readings < 70, nadir 41. Hour-01 TBR 18.5% suggests elevated low risk overnight. Hour-19 spike post-afternoon TAR peak (hour 16 32.1%) consistent with overaggressive loop correction (detects high IOB, suppresses basal/issues negative SMB, creates low by hour 19). Profile change 2026-08-13 21:23:31 preceded lows same day/next day (temporal association, causation unconfirmed). Loop aggressively suppresses afternoon high via SMB accumulation, creating IOB tail into evening, then high-to-low oscillation. Basal segments 00:00 (0.6 U/h) and 19:00 (0.7 U/h) may exacerbate (timing mismatch with low-risk hours), but IOB/meal dynamics are likely primary driver.

issues.title: ISF model discrepancy: declared 56 mg/dL/U vs. observed effective 150–180 mg/dL/U from therapy_response_windows (glucose_change / insulin_units).
issues.description: 24 bolus events show glucose_change / insulin_units ranges 36–353 mg/dL/U (extreme spread due to meal/IOB confound, but median ~150–180 after excluding extremes). Declared single FLAT ISF segment 56 mg/dL/U (Dynamic ISF 70% brings effective to ~80). Interpretation: either (a) declared ISF 56 is too low (insulin weaker than profile assumes), or (b) therapy response range is confounded by meal IOB overlap (cannot separate ISF from meal effect without carbs). Cannot finalize ISF change until carb logging clarifies bolus response to known carb amounts. However, conservatism is evident (micro-SMB 0.05 U per cycle, Dynamic ISF 70% reducing bolus), suggesting loop is being very cautious—consistent with ISF being too low (low ISF = weak insulin = small bolus to avoid overshoot).

issues.title: Hour-01 TBR 18.5% (elevated low risk midnight) and hour-16 basal drop 0.7→0.5 U/h during peak TAR 32.1% (counterintuitive).
issues.description: Hour-01 TBR 18.5% (avg 90.6 mg/dL, target 90) suggests basal 0.6 U/h (00:00 segment, lowest in profile) may be too low, or residual evening IOB from corrections overshoots into midnight low. Hour-16 TAR 32.1% occurs exactly when basal drops from 0.7 to 0.5 U/h (–29%). However, basal-alone explanation implausible: basal constant 0.5 U/h hours 16–18, but TAR varies hour-16 (32.1%) → hour-17 (22.6%) → hour-18 (11.9%), showing TAR is meal-dynamics-driven. Hour-01 and hour-19 TBR spikes likely driven by IOB oscillation (high → correction → low), not basal magnitude. Basal timing assessment deferred until carb logging and ISF changes clarify meal/bolus patterns.

issues.title: Profile declared 2026-08-13 21:23:31 (8 days old at analysis); lows occurred immediately after (2026-08-13 17:04–17:14, 2026-08-14 18:04–18:14).

Glucose extremes show lows on 2026-08-13 (nadir 42) and 2026-08-14 (nadir 41), occurring 4–6 hours post-profile-change declaration or within ~24h post-profile application. Lows may have triggered profile review, or profile change was applied earlier on 2026-08-13 and declared later. Either way, system may not yet be stable (only 8 days post-profile). Recommend delaying major ISF/basal changes 1–2 weeks from profile date to allow stabilization. Profile change is recent; observed patterns (afternoon TAR, midnight/evening lows) may reflect transient adjustment rather than true settings mismatch.

recommendations.title: Enable carb logging (Nightscout treatment entries) immediately for all meals and snacks; log carb amount (grams) and meal time. Continue for minimum 7 days to establish baseline.
recommendations.description: Zero carbs logged (14-day) prevents CR validation, COB-based SMB, and meal timing clarity. Carb logging is lowest-risk, highest-information change. Expected benefit: (1) Loop gains meal context (COB > 0 during meals). (2) After 7 days, enables empirical ISF verification via bolus_response_to_carbs (glucose_change / (carbs_grams / CR) = actual ISF). (3) Clarifies meal timing for prebolus assessment (meal log time vs. bolus time gap). (4) Identifies slow-absorbing meals for e-carb consideration. (5) Earlier meal detection (carb entry triggers alertness vs. UAM delay). User burden: 1–2 min per meal (write carbs, enter in app). After 7 days, review therapy response windows; compare bolus timing and glucose rise patterns to baseline. Proceed to ISF assessment only after carb-logging data is available.

recommendations.title: After carb logging is stable (7+ days), enable smb_with_cob_enabled=true (currently false) to allow COB-based SMB detection and earlier meal bolus triggering.
recommendations.description: Currently smb_with_cob_enabled=false because zero carbs logged (COB always 0). Once carbs are logged, COB will be > 0 during meals, enabling COB-based SMB (loop triggers bolus when carbs are logged, not waiting for glucose rise). Expected benefit: 30–60 min earlier meal detection, reducing glucose overshoot. Contingent on step 1 (carb logging enabled). Do not enable smb_with_cob_enabled until carbs are actively logged (no benefit if COB stays 0).

recommendations.title: After 7 days of carb logging, empirically verify ISF direction by calculating implied ISF from bolus response: ISF = glucose_change_mg_dl / (carbs_grams / CR_g_per_unit). Compare result to declared 56. If implied ISF > 100 mg/dL/U, declared 56 is too low; consider increase toward 80–120 mg/dL/U, testing incrementally. If implied ISF < 60 mg/dL/U, declared 56 may be appropriate; assess if micro-SMB strategy or Dynamic ISF reduction is the actual limiting factor.
recommendations.description: Declared ISF 56 vs. observed therapy_response_windows 150–180 discrepancy cannot be resolved without carbs. Carb logging will enable empirical ISF verification: for each logged meal, calculate total bolus from CR (carbs / CR), compare to glucose change, derive implied ISF. If multiple meals show implied ISF 100–150, declared 56 is too low. ISF direction (increase vs. decrease) affects bolus formula: higher ISF = less sensitive insulin = smaller bolus per glucose rise (oref1 formula: bolus = rise / ISF). Currently, therapy windows show very conservative boluses (0.05 U per 3-min cycle); if ISF 56 is correct, micro-bolus strategy is appropriate for safety. If ISF 56 is too high (insulin more sensitive than profile assumes), boluses should be larger, and observed micro-bolus is undersized. Only carb-logged data can clarify. Do not change ISF until carb data is available.

recommendations.title: After ISF and carb logging are stable (1–2 weeks, ~2026-09-02 to 2026-09-04), conduct fasting basal test (no meals, 6–8 hours, minimal SMB) to isolate basal effects on hour-01 and hour-16 anomalies. Do not change basal until fasting test data confirms basal inadequacy (vs. IOB/meal effect).
recommendations.description: Hour-01 TBR 18.5% and hour-16 basal drop coincide with meal windows and IOB oscillation; basal-alone explanation implausible. Fasting test will clarify: if glucose is flat (±10 mg/dL over 6–8h), basal is adequate. If glucose drifts up or down consistently, basal segment adjustment is needed. Schedule on rest day, inform care team, have fast-acting carbs available. Delay until ISF and carb logging are stable (to avoid IOB tail from prior meal during test). Test each basal segment separately (midnight, early morning, afternoon, evening).

recommendations.title: After carb logging is routine (7+ days), assess prebolus feasibility by reviewing therapy response windows: measure time from bolus issuance to glucose peak (target < 2 hours, vs. current 2–4 hours). If user can log carbs 5–10 min before meal, enable prebolus by allowing loop to issue bolus at carb entry time (requires smb_with_cob_enabled=true and carb entry before meal). If user logs carbs after eating (reactive), prebolus is not feasible without manual intervention.
recommendations.description: Current therapy_response_windows show all boluses at or after glucose rise; no prebolus observed. Reactive bolus (glucose rises, then bolus issued) causes overshoot before bolus IOB peaks. Prebolus (bolus 10–15 min before carbs arrive) would suppress rise in real-time. Feasibility depends on user willingness to log carbs prospectively. If user can do so, loop will auto-prebolus once carbs are logged (COB-triggered SMB). If not, accept reactive-only bolus (safe, just slower control).

recommendations.title: After carb logging shows slow-absorbing meals (glucose rise > 3 hours, peaks at 240m or later), implement e-carbs selectively for those meals. Example: 'Lunch 80g carbs: 50g immediate, 30g e-carbs 2h' (split bolus, extended tail matching absorption time).
recommendations.description: Therapy_response_windows show 4-hour glucose rises on 2026-08-14 and 2026-08-15 (coinciding with GLP-1 doses), consistent with delayed absorption. Standard bolus (immediate only) completes insulin effect before carbs peak, creating low-IOB-high-glucose-rise phase and rebound highs (e.g., 2026-08-15: drop to 94 mg/dL at 120m, rebound to 188 at 240m). E-carbs extend bolus timing to match absorption. GLP-1 slows gastric emptying; confirm effect via carb-logging data (compare meal absorption on GLP-1 days vs. non-GLP-1 days). Implement e-carbs only for confirmed slow meals (need 2–3 examples); do not use all meals (fast meals with e-carbs cause lows).

profile_recommendation.recommendation: Keep declared ISF 56 mg/dL/U and all basal segments unchanged for now. Enable carb logging immediately (step 1). After 7 days of carb-logged meal data, recalculate empirical ISF using bolus response to known carbs (ISF = glucose_change / (carbs / CR)). Use empirical ISF to determine if ISF change is warranted: if implied ISF > 100, increase declared ISF incrementally toward 80–120 mg/dL/U; if implied ISF < 60, keep ISF unchanged and address meal bolus strategy (prebolus, immediate bolus % increase) instead. ISF change is the most impactful profile adjustment for afternoon hyperglycemia (hour-16 TAR 32.1%), but direction and magnitude cannot be determined until carb logging provides empirical reference. Delaying ISF change 1–2 weeks is lower-risk than guessing based on confounded therapy responses (meal/IOB overlap).
profile_recommendation.rationale: Declared ISF 56 vs. observed therapy_response_windows 150–180 discrepancy is unresolvable without carbs (IOB subtraction in algorithm vs. pure ISF effect unknown). Carb logging will enable empirical verification via bolus response to logged meal carbs. Profile declared 2026-08-13 (8 days old at analysis); lows occurred immediately post-profile; system may not yet be stable. Recommend 1–2 week stabilization before major profile changes. Carb logging is prerequisite for all downstream decisions (ISF, prebolus, e-carbs); implement first. Afternoon hyperglycemia (TAR 32.1%) is primary issue, and ISF is likely contributor, but empirical data (carb-logged bolus response) is required to confirm ISF direction and magnitude before change. Safety: larger ISF (if change is warranted) increases bolus size and IOB, increasing low risk; justify only with clear carb-logged evidence.
profile_recommendation.next_check: After 7 days of carb logging (dates ~2026-08-28 to 2026-09-04): (1) Calculate implied ISF for each meal: for logged meal carbs, divide total glucose change (peak BG − pre-meal BG) by (carbs_grams / CR_segment). Example: if breakfast 50g carbs, CR 13 g/U, total bolus should be 3.8 U; if glucose rises from 95 to 160 (change 65 mg/dL) with bolus 0.3 U immediate + 3.5 U SMB cumulative = 3.8 U total, then implied ISF = 65 / 3.8 ≈ 17 mg/dL/U (very high sensitivity, unusual, suggests confound). Correct calculation: glucose_change / insulin_delivered_by_loop (not CR-predicted). (2) Compare empirical ISF from step 1 to declared 56: if > 100 mg/dL/U, declared 56 is too low; increase toward 80–120. If < 60 mg/dL/U, keep 56. If 60–100 mg/dL/U, assess afternoon TAR separately (may be meal bolus strategy issue, not ISF). (3) Measure afternoon TAR (hour 16) after 7 days carb logging (before ISF change): if carb logging alone (without ISF change) reduces TAR from 32.1% to < 25%, carb logging and earlier meal detection are effective; defer ISF change pending next step (step 4 review). If TAR remains > 28%, ISF change is likely needed; proceed with step 4 (ISF adjustment based on empirical data).

parameter_decisions.rationale: Hour-01 TBR 18.5% (elevated low risk) may suggest basal 0.6 U/h (lowest in profile) is too low. However, hour-01 TBR coincides with residual evening IOB from corrections (profile change 2026-08-13 may have altered correction bolus sizing) and oscillatory glucose patterns (afternoon high → evening aggressive correction → midnight low). Basal-alone explanation is not primary. Keep 0.6 U/h unchanged until carb logging and ISF assessment are complete; then conduct fasting basal test (recommendation 3) to isolate basal effect on hour-01 TBR. If fasting test shows consistent glucose drift in midnight hours, increase 0.6 U/h to 0.65–0.7 U/h.
00:00→05:00 transition (0.6 → 0.7 U/h) shows hours 04–07 excellent stability (TIR 95–98.7%, TBR 1.3–4.8%). Basal at 0.7 U/h is appropriate for early morning. Keep unchanged.

05:00→10:00 transition (0.7 → 0.8 U/h, highest basal rate). Hours 06–10 show breakfast window with hour-08 excellent (98.2% TIR), hours 09–10 elevated TAR consistent with meal absorption (not basal issue). Keep 0.8 U/h; problem is meal bolus, not basal.

10:00 onward (0.8 → 0.7 U/h transition, modest decrease). Hours 11–12 show elevated glucose (TAR 7.5–14%) consistent with breakfast/lunch overlap and meal bolus inadequacy, not basal issue. Keep 0.7 U/h.

16:00 onward (0.7 → 0.5 U/h, –29% drop at peak afternoon TAR 32.1%). Drop is counterintuitive (glucose high, basal decreases). However, basal-only explanation implausible: basal constant 0.5 U/h hours 16–18, but TAR varies hour-16 (32.1%) → hour-17 (22.6%) → hour-18 (11.9%), showing TAR is meal-driven. Do not change basal without carb logging and ISF assessment. After meal strategy is optimized, if afternoon TAR remains high, re-evaluate whether 0.5 U/h should be reduced (e.g., 0.7 U/h, revert to pre-16:00 rate).

16:00→18:00 segment (0.5 U/h). 18:00 onward (0.5 → 0.6 U/h, +20% increase). Hour-18 shows elevated glucose tail (avg 124.2, TAR 11.9%) from afternoon meal, hour-19 TBR spike (15.3%, avg 105.4). Basal increase from 0.5 to 0.6 U/h is modest. Hour-19 TBR spike is overcorrection pattern (loop aggressively suppressing afternoon-elevated glucose via SMB + zero temp basal, creating low by 19:00), not basal issue. Keep 0.6 U/h; address meal bolus and IOB dynamics first.
18:00→19:00 transition (0.6 → 0.7 U/h). Hours 20–21 show recovery (TIR 88.6%, 92.3%, avg 117–120). Basal at 0.7 U/h is appropriate for evening recovery. Keep unchanged.

CR cannot be validated without carb entries (zero carbs logged). Declared 13 g/U is reasonable for T1D. CR is currently bypassed (UAM-only micro-SMB strategy). Keep CR segments unchanged until carb logging is enabled for 7+ days; then review actual bolus response to logged carbs and adjust CR if needed. Do not change CR until carb data provides empirical reference.
CR 04:00 segment 11.1 g/U (more sensitive than 00:00 13 g/U). Early morning sensitivity variation is plausible. Keep unchanged; await carb logging for validation.
CR 08:00 segment 13.2 g/U (breakfast, similar to midnight). Keep unchanged; await carb logging.

CR 16:00 segment 10.5 g/U (most sensitive, lowest). Afternoon hyperglycemia (hour-16 TAR 32.1%) is NOT due to CR being too insensitive (10.5 g/U is sensitive); issue is ISF 56 (too low or confounded) and micro-SMB strategy. Keep CR unchanged; address ISF after carb logging.
CR 20:00 segment 12.6 g/U (evening/dinner). Keep unchanged; await carb logging.

ISF 56 vs. therapy_response_windows glucose_change / insulin_units ~150–180 represents major discrepancy. Interpretation depends on oref1 formula and whether therapy response is confounded by meal/IOB overlap (cannot separate without carbs). Two hypotheses: (H1) declared ISF 56 is too low (insulin weaker than profile assumes), bolus undersizes, afternoon TAR rises; solution: increase ISF toward 80–120. (H2) declared ISF 56 is correct; therapy response range 150–180 is artifact of meal/IOB overlap; solution: keep ISF, address meal bolus strategy (prebolus, immediate % increase). Cannot resolve until carb logging provides empirical bolus response to known carbs. Keep ISF 56 unchanged. After 7 days of carb logging, calculate implied ISF (glucose_change / (carbs / CR)); use result to inform direction (increase vs. decrease). Do not guess; empirical data required.

Overnight target 90 mg/dL is low but reasonable for closed-loop T1D (safety margin above hypo). Hour-01 TBR 18.5% suggests target may be tight; however, TBR spike is likely IOB-driven (residual correction bolus), not target-driven. Keep 90 mg/dL for now; after basal test (recommendation 3), may increase to 95–100 mg/dL if TBR improves.
Breakfast target 100 mg/dL (10 mg/dL higher than overnight, allowing for meal absorption). Hour-08 TIR 98.2% excellent; target is appropriate. Keep.
Evening target 90 mg/dL (transition from 100 at 08:00 back to 90 at 23:00, matching overnight). Reasonable. Keep.

DIA 10 hours is appropriate for dilute u200 insulin (profile note confirms). Bolus recovery patterns in therapy_response_windows mostly consistent with 10h DIA (glucose recovers by 4–6h post-bolus; IOB visible in loop snapshots through 6–10h). Cannot refine without carb logging and fasting bolus test, but no evidence contradicts 10h. Keep. After fasting basal test (recommendation 3), observe bolus effect in isolation at 6–8h post-bolus to refine DIA if needed.

SMB and UAM enabled and functional (24 loop snapshots show active SMB every 3 min). Micro-bolus pattern (0.05 U per cycle) is conservative but appropriate given zero carbs logged. Keep SMB and UAM enabled. After carb logging enabled (recommendation 1), enable smb_with_cob_enabled=true (recommendation 2) to allow COB-based SMB. But do not disable smb_enabled or uam_enabled overall.

parameter_decisions.suggested_value: smb_always_enabled=true; smb_with_cob_enabled=true (after carb logging enabled); smb_with_carbs_enabled=false; smb_with_temp_target_enabled=true; smb_with_high_temp_target_enabled=false
parameter_decisions.rationale: Current: smb_with_cob_enabled=false (SMB does not activate when COB > 0) because zero carbs logged; COB always 0. After carb logging enabled (recommendation 1), smb_with_cob_enabled should be changed to true (enable SMB on COB detection, earlier meal detection than UAM delay). Decision: VERIFY. After carb logging is active for 2–3 days, user should enable smb_with_cob_enabled=true. This is a conditional change dependent on carb logging status; cannot be done now. Other conditions appropriate (smb_always_enabled true, smb_with_carbs_enabled false, smb_with_temp_target_enabled true, smb_with_high_temp_target_enabled false).

parameter_decisions.current_value: smb_interval_minutes=3 min; max_smb_basal_minutes=15 min; max_uam_smb_basal_minutes=20 min
parameter_decisions.rationale: Current SMB settings are standard and functional. smb_interval_minutes=3 is typical (frequent SMB, avoids large per-cycle IOB). max_smb_basal_minutes=15 and max_uam_smb_basal_minutes=20 are reasonable conservative limits. Observed boluses 0.05–0.25 U per cycle are consistent with these limits. Do not change SMB delivery settings now. After carb logging and ISF assessment are complete (1–2 weeks), re-evaluate: if afternoon TAR remains high despite larger ISF (if ISF is increased), consider increasing max_smb_basal_minutes to 20–25 (allow larger per-cycle bolus). If low risk increases after ISF change, keep current limits.

parameter_decisions.parameter: AAPS / max basal and max IOB limits
parameter_decisions.rationale: max_basal_u_per_hour=12 U/h is 15–24× current basal (0.5–0.8); safe ceiling, not reached. max_iob_units=25 U is conservative (1.56× daily basal ~16 U); not reached (max IOB observed 4.73 U). Both appropriate. Keep unchanged. After ISF increase (if warranted by carb logging), monitor IOB in loop snapshots; if IOB regularly exceeds 20 U, may increase max_iob_units to 30–35 U, but do not change now.

Current Dynamic ISF 70% is conservative (effective ISF ~80 from declared 56). After carb logging clarifies ISF direction, may adjust Dynamic ISF to modulate effective ISF, but defer change until ISF is clarified. Autosens remains disabled (appropriate for profile stabilization phase; profile only 8 days old at analysis). Keep autosens_raises_target and autosens_lowers_target false. Do not change sensitivity settings until carb logging provides empirical ISF reference and profile is stable (1–2 weeks post-profile-change date 2026-08-13).

Current settings standard and appropriate. min_5m_carbimpact=8 is oref1 default; should detect typical meal-driven glucose rises. meal_max_absorption_hours=7 is standard (allows extended meals and e-carbs up to 7h). No change needed now. Decision: VERIFY after carb logging enabled. Once carbs are logged, review UAM detection (does loop correctly identify meal starts?) and glucose rise patterns (do slopes match min_5m_carbimpact threshold?). If UAM misses meals (glucose rises but SMB not issued), decrease min_5m_carbimpact to 5 (more sensitive). If UAM over-detects (SMB on non-meal rises), increase to 10 (less sensitive). For now, keep both at current values.

meal_strategy_summary.suggestion: Maintain current UAM-driven progressive micro-bolus strategy (no prebolus, 4–20% immediate bolus, 80–96% via SMB every 3 min, no e-carbs) through carb-logging phase (7+ days). Once carb logging is active and stable, transition to COB-based strategy: (1) Enable smb_with_cob_enabled=true (allow SMB triggered by logged carbs, earlier detection). (2) Assess prebolus feasibility: if user logs carbs 5–10 min before eating, loop will auto-prebolus; if logs reactively (during/after meal), prebolus not feasible. (3) Target increase immediate bolus % from current 4–20% to 30–50% by reducing per-cycle SMB cap and increasing ISF (after carb logging determines ISF direction). (4) Add e-carbs selectively for slow-absorbing meals (glucose rise > 3 hours, typically GLP-1 dose days). Overall goal: reduce afternoon TAR from 32.1% to < 20%, maintain TBR < 5%, achieve TIR > 90%.
meal_strategy_summary.rationale: Current strategy (UAM-only, micro-bolus, reactive) is safe but inefficient (glucose high 1–4 hours during meal, then oscillation into low from overcorrection). Carb logging will unlock three improvements: (1) COB detection (meal-specific, not UAM waitfor-rise delay), (2) prebolus timing (bolus 10–15 min before meal), (3) meal composition knowledge (identify slow meals for e-carbs). Sequential strategy (maintain current 7+ days, then transition) minimizes risk. Expected glucose impact: (a) COB enablement → 30–60 min earlier detection, reducing overshoot ~30 mg/dL. (b) Prebolus → additional 15 min bolus IOB before carbs, reducing peak ~20–40 mg/dL. (c) Larger immediate % (30–50% vs. 4–20%) → faster suppression, reducing time-to-peak from 2–4h to 1–2h. (d) E-carbs for slow meals → prevent rebound highs. Combined: TIR 86% → 90–95%, TAR 8.9% → 5–8%, TBR 5.1% → 3–4%. Dependency: recommendations 1 (carb logging) and ISF verification (from profile_recommendation) must precede meal strategy transition.
meal_strategy_summary.next_observation: After 7 days of carb logging (~2026-08-28 to 2026-09-04): (1) Measure bolus-to-peak lag (bolus time to glucose peak); target < 2h vs. current 2–4h. If lag reduces from carb logging + COB enablement alone, loop is benefiting from earlier detection. (2) Measure immediate bolus % of total: (immediate_bolus) / (immediate + SMB_cumulative × 3min_cycles). Target 30–50% vs. current 4–20%. (3) Identify slow meals: glucose rise > 3h, peak at 240m+. Check for GLP-1 dose timing (lags meal?). Log carb composition if available (high fat, high fiber). (4) Check if prebolus is feasible: do therapy response windows show carbs logged 5–10 min before bolus (prospective, enabling prebolus), or 0–5 min before/after (retrospective, reactive only)? Most impactful observation: measure bolus-to-peak lag post-carb-logging. If lag reduces to < 2h without other changes, carb logging + COB enablement is working; proceed to ISF verification (next step). If lag remains 2–4h despite COB enablement, user is logging retrospectively, and prebolus requires manual bolus at carb entry.

exceptions.pattern: Large manual bolus exception: 2.4 U on 2026-08-15 11:25 (1 of 24 events, 4%). Start BG elevated 181, bolus caused strong drop –87 in 120m, rebound by 240m.
exceptions.suggestion: Classify as user manual override when loop micro-SMB is insufficient. After carb logging and ISF verification, review if exception persists. If user continues manual override for anticipated large meals, consider: (1) increase max_smb_basal_minutes or max_iob_units to allow loop to auto-bolus larger, or (2) support manual bolus efficiently (user logs 'large meal' or high carb amount, loop issues larger auto-bolus, user confirms or overrides). Do not force loop to larger SMB if user prefers manual control; respect user preference.
exceptions.rationale: One large manual bolus suggests user can override loop (not mechanically blocked). After ISF increase and carb logging, loop may auto-bolus larger amounts, reducing need for manual override. If override persists, it is user preference. Support by enabling efficient manual override (carb logging signals meal size to loop).

exceptions.pattern: Slow glucose absorption (4-hour rise on 2026-08-14 and 2026-08-15, coinciding with GLP-1 doses 2026-08-14 08:14). Peak glucose reaches 235–293 mg/dL despite micro-SMB.
exceptions.suggestion: After carb logging is active, stratify meal absorption by GLP-1 dose timing. If glucose rise is consistently slower (> 3 hours) on GLP-1 days, use e-carbs for those meals: split bolus into (a) immediate bolus for fast carbs (50% of total CR), (b) e-carbs extending 3–4 hours for slow carbs (50% of total CR, duration 180–240 min). Do not implement e-carbs until GLP-1 effect is confirmed via carb-logging data (need 2+ GLP-1 dose days with carbs logged).
exceptions.rationale: GLP-1 slows gastric emptying, delaying meal absorption (4h vs. 2h typical). Standard bolus (immediate only) completes insulin effect before carbs peak, creating low-IOB-high-rise phase and rebound high (2026-08-15: drop 94 at 120m, rebound 188 at 240m). E-carbs extend bolus to match absorption, flattening response. Implement only after GLP-1 effect is confirmed and baseline carb logging established.

implementation_steps.title: Enable carb logging immediately (next meal, 2026-08-21 onward). Log all carbs and snacks in Nightscout treatment entries with carb amount (grams) and meal time.
implementation_steps.rationale: Zero carbs logged prevents CR validation, COB-based SMB, meal timing clarity. Carb logging is lowest-risk, highest-information change. User burden: 1–2 min per meal.
implementation_steps.verification: After 2–3 days: verify carb entries appear in Nightscout and loop algorithm inputs (COB visible in AAPS logs). If carbs logged, proceed to step 2.

implementation_steps.title: Monitor glucose control for 3–5 days post-carb-logging without changing settings. Observe therapy response windows; measure bolus timing vs. glucose peak lag (target < 2h vs. current 2–4h). No automation changes during this baseline phase.
implementation_steps.rationale: Carb logging alone may improve glucose by earlier meal detection (UAM context, even without COB-based SMB enabled). Establish baseline for carb-logging impact before ISF or other changes.
implementation_steps.verification: After 3–5 days: measure bolus-to-peak lag and afternoon TAR. If TAR improves to 25–28%, carb logging alone has 4–7% impact. If unchanged, ISF or meal bolus strategy is likely limiting factor.

implementation_steps.title: After carb-logging baseline (step 2, ~2026-08-25), enable smb_with_cob_enabled=true (currently false). This allows SMB triggered by logged carbs (COB > 0) instead of UAM only.
implementation_steps.rationale: COB-based SMB will trigger bolus when carbs are logged (earlier than UAM), reducing meal detection delay. Expected benefit: 30–60 min earlier bolus, reducing glucose overshoot.
implementation_steps.verification: After 2–3 days of smb_with_cob_enabled=true: measure bolus-to-peak lag. If reduces from 2–4h to 1–2h, COB enablement is effective. If unchanged, user may be logging reactively (too late for prebolus benefit).

implementation_steps.title: After carb logging is stable (7+ days, ~2026-08-28 to 2026-09-04), empirically verify ISF by calculating implied ISF from bolus response to logged carbs. Formula: ISF = glucose_change_mg_dl / (carbs_grams / CR_g_per_unit). Compare implied ISF to declared 56.
implementation_steps.rationale: Therapy response windows show 150–180 mg/dL/U, vs. declared 56; discrepancy cannot resolve without carbs. Carb logging provides empirical reference for ISF direction (increase vs. decrease).
implementation_steps.verification: If implied ISF > 100 mg/dL/U from 2+ meals, declared 56 is likely too low; consider increase toward 80–120 mg/dL/U (test incrementally). If implied ISF < 60 mg/dL/U, declared 56 may be appropriate; assess if meal bolus strategy (prebolus, immediate %) is the limiting factor. If implied ISF 60–100 mg/dL/U, keep 56 and focus on meal strategy.

implementation_steps.title: If step 4 (empirical ISF) shows implied ISF > 100, schedule ISF change: increase declared ISF from 56 toward 80–100 mg/dL/U (conservative first step), test for 3–5 days. Measure afternoon TAR (target < 20%+) and TBR (maintain < 5%). Do not change other settings simultaneously.
implementation_steps.rationale: If implied ISF is significantly higher than declared 56, micro-bolus undersizing is likely. Larger ISF will increase oref1 bolus formula output, enabling larger SMB per cycle.
implementation_steps.verification: After 3–5 days of ISF increase: if TAR improves to 20–25% and TBR remains stable (< 5%), change is successful. If TAR improves < 5% despite ISF increase, meal timing (prebolus) may be limiting factor; proceed to step 6. If TBR increases to > 8%, ISF increase is too aggressive; revert and try smaller increase (65 or 70 mg/dL/U).

implementation_steps.title: After ISF change is validated (or if ISF change shows TAR remains > 20%), assess prebolus feasibility: review therapy response windows; measure bolus issuance time vs. meal logged time (if user logs carbs prospectively, loop can prebolus; if logs retrospectively, prebolus is manual only).
implementation_steps.rationale: Current reactive bolus (after glucose rises) causes overshoot. Prebolus 10–15 min before meal would suppress rise. Feasibility depends on user willingness to log carbs early.
implementation_steps.verification: If therapy response windows show carbs logged 5–10 min before bolus (prospective), prebolus is enabled automatically (smb_with_cob_enabled=true will trigger bolus at carb entry time). If logs reactively (during/after meal, 0–5 min before/after bolus), manual prebolus is user choice (log carbs, manually bolus 10 min before eating).

implementation_steps.title: If afternoon TAR remains > 20% after steps 4–6 (ISF verification, possible increase, prebolus assessment), identify slow-absorbing meals (glucose rise > 3 hours, peaks at 240m+) and implement e-carbs for those meals. Example: 'Lunch 80g: 50g immediate, 30g e-carbs 2h' (split bolus extending 120+ minutes).
implementation_steps.rationale: GLP-1-induced slow absorption (4 hours on GLP-1 dose days) causes bolus IOB to peak before carbs peak, creating low–rebound–high oscillation. E-carbs extend bolus timing to match absorption.
implementation_steps.verification: After e-carbs for slow meals (5–7 days): measure glucose peak height and rebound pattern. Target: peak 20–30 mg/dL lower than non-e-carb meals of similar size, no rebound (flat tail). If rebound eliminated, e-carbs working; refine amount/duration if needed. If rebound persists, e-carb timing may be off; adjust.

implementation_steps.title: After all changes implemented and stable (~2026-09-07 onward, 2–3 weeks post-analysis), conduct fasting basal test: no meals, 6–8 hours, minimal SMB. Test each basal segment separately (midnight, early morning, afternoon, evening). Expected result: flat glucose ±10 mg/dL during fast.
implementation_steps.rationale: Fasting test isolates basal effect from meal/bolus/IOB. Hour-01 TBR 18.5% and hour-16 anomalies may be meal/IOB-driven, not basal. Test clarifies.
implementation_steps.verification: For each fasting segment: plot glucose over 6–8 hours. If flat (±5 mg/dL), basal adequate. If drifts up > 20 mg/dL over 6h, basal too low; increase by 10–20%. If drifts down > 20 mg/dL, basal too high; decrease by 10–20%. Make single basal segment changes; retest after 2–3 days.

education.topic: Why carb logging is essential for closed-loop optimization
education.content: Carbohydrate logging links your meals to your insulin pump. Without carb entries, the loop uses only glucose rise (UAM = unannounced meal detection) to detect meals, which means it is always 10–30 minutes behind. With carb logging, the loop knows when and how much carbs are arriving and can issue insulin before glucose rises, preventing highs. Carb logging also enables personalized bolus calculations using carb ratios (CR = how many grams of carbs one unit of insulin covers). Currently, your pump uses a 'safe guess' strategy (small SMB every 3 minutes) because it does not know meal sizes. Carb logging upgrades to personalized strategy. Time burden: 1–2 minutes per meal. Benefit: better glucose control, fewer highs and lows, faster meal response.

education.topic: Understanding ISF (Insulin Sensitivity Factor) and your glucose patterns
education.content: ISF is how much your blood glucose drops per unit of insulin. The profile says ISF=56, meaning 1 unit of insulin should lower glucose by 56 mg/dL. Looking at your actual bolus responses over 14 days, the data suggests your insulin may act like ISF=150–180 (1 unit lowers glucose 150–180 mg/dL). This mismatch means the pump thinks your insulin is weaker than reality, so it holds back on bolus size to avoid lows. Result: afternoon glucose stays high (32% of time, peak 293). The discrepancy cannot be resolved until carb logging shows how much glucose actually changes in response to known carb amounts. After 7 days of carb logging, we will calculate true ISF from your meal responses and determine if ISF needs to increase.

education.topic: Prebolus timing: why bolusing before eating improves control
education.content: Prebolus means giving insulin 10–15 minutes before you eat, so insulin is already acting when carbs arrive. Currently, your boluses are reactive (given after glucose is already rising), which means glucose spikes first, then insulin catches up. Prebolus flattens the spike. Example: if you eat breakfast at 8:00 and bolus at 7:50 (10 min early), your glucose may peak at 130 instead of 160. To enable prebolus with your loop (AAPS), you must log carbs 5–10 minutes before eating. If you can do so, the loop will auto-prebolus when carbs are entered (if smb_with_cob_enabled=true). If you always log after eating, prebolus is not possible without manual intervention.

education.topic: Extended carbs (e-carbs): when to use them for slow-absorbing meals
education.content: Extended carbs (e-carbs) tell the pump a meal is being absorbed slowly (over 2–4 hours instead of 1–2 hours). This happens with fatty, high-fiber meals, or when on GLP-1 medication (which slows stomach emptying). Without e-carbs, the pump issues all bolus upfront, peaks before carbs finish arriving, causing a low around 2 hours, then high rebound 3–4 hours later. With e-carbs, you split the bolus: some now, some extended over 2–3 hours matching carbs. Example: 'Lunch 80g carbs: 50g regular, 30g e-carbs over 2 hours' means bolus for 50g now, then add insulin gradually for the remaining 30g. Result: flatter glucose, no low-rebound. You are on GLP-1, which may slow your meal absorption; after carb logging shows which meals are slow-absorbing, e-carbs can help those meals specifically. Do not use e-carbs for all meals (only slow ones); fast meals with e-carbs cause lows.

education.topic: Why single-variable testing (changing one setting at a time) is critical
education.content: If you change ISF, basal, and Dynamic ISF all at once, and glucose improves, you will not know which change helped. If glucose worsens (e.g., lows increase), you will not know which caused it. This is confounding. Safe tuning means changing ONE setting at a time, waiting 3–5 days to see effect, then deciding: keep, modify, or revert. Example: step 3 reduces Dynamic ISF from 70 to 50 first. Wait 3 days. If TAR improves, good—keep it. If TAR is still high, then we know ISF (not Dynamic ISF) is the issue. Single-variable testing takes longer (1–2 weeks vs. 1 day to change everything), but gives safe, clear answers.

safety_notes.content: This analysis is decision-support content only. You (and your care team: clinician, diabetes educator, pump trainer) must independently verify every proposed change, understand the rationale, and agree before implementation. TuneMyBG does not provide medical advice, diagnose, or treat any condition. You are solely responsible for safe operation of your insulin pump, glucose monitoring, and diabetes management. All changes must comply with AAPS safety limits, pump manufacturer guidance, and local diabetes care standards.

Make changes in the sequence recommended (steps 1–8). Do not skip steps or change multiple settings simultaneously. For example: (1) Start carb logging alone; do not change ISF or basal at the same time. (2) After carb logging is stable, then enable smb_with_cob_enabled; do not also change declared ISF. (3) Only after ISF direction is clarified by carb-logged data, consider ISF change. If you deviate from this sequence, you will create ambiguity about which change caused improvement or harm, making future tuning harder.

Monitor glucose closely during and after each change. Have fast-acting carbs (glucose tablets, juice, candy) available. If any of these occur, immediately revert the last change and contact your care team: (1) Time below 70 mg/dL increases above 10% (daily average), or single reading drops below 50 mg/dL. (2) Time above 180 mg/dL increases above 15% (change worsened control). (3) Erratic glucose swings (> 100 mg/dL in 30 min) or inability to stabilize glucose despite multiple boluses. (4) Symptoms of hypoglycemia (shakiness, dizziness, confusion) even if CGM reading is > 70 mg/dL (possible CGM lag). (5) Pump or CGM alarms/errors preventing normal operation.

Carb logging requires 1–2 minutes per meal (estimate grams, enter in app). Some users find this sustainable; others find it burdensome. If carb logging feels overwhelming, discuss with your diabetes educator about simplified logging (e.g., 'small, medium, large meal' instead of exact grams), or reduced frequency (e.g., 3 meals + 1 snack, not every snack). Carb logging is essential for this plan, but your sustainability and quality of life must be respected. If you cannot sustain carb logging, discuss alternative strategies with your care team.

This can confound glucose patterns (slower rise = loop thinks meal is smaller = under-boluses). After carb logging, you will see which meals are slow-absorbing (likely those after or near GLP-1 doses). E-carbs (step 7) are the tool for slow meals. Do not assume all meals are slow; carb logging will clarify. GLP-1 can suppress appetite, so you may eat smaller meals or skip snacks. Log accurately what you actually eat, not what you 'should' eat.

Step 8 (fasting basal test) involves 6–8 hours without eating, with only basal and SMB running. This is safe only if: (1) Pump is functioning normally (no errors/warnings). (2) CGM is accurate (no sensor errors or gaps). (3) You are supervised or in contact with care team. (4) Prior glucose patterns show TBR is low (< 8%), so fasting is unlikely to cause severe low. Do not attempt fasting test if: TBR is currently high (> 8%), you are ill, or you are driving/working and cannot monitor closely. Schedule on a rest day, inform your care team, and have a plan to treat low if needed (fast-acting carbs available).
